# Psalm 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the music director. To the tune of 'Doe of the Dawn.' A psalm of David.

**2** My God, my God, why have You abandoned me? Why are You so far away when I groan for help?

**3** Every day I call to You, my God, but You do not answer. Every night I lift my voice, but I find no relief.

**4** Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.

**5** Our ancestors trusted in You, and You rescued them.

**6** They cried out to You and were saved. They trusted in You and were never disgraced.

**7** But I am a worm and not a man. I am scorned and despised by all.

**8** Everyone who sees me mocks me. They sneer and shake their heads, saying,

**9** "Is this the one who relies on the LORD? Then let the LORD save him! If the LORD loves him so much, let Him rescue him!"

**10** Yet You brought me safely from my mother's womb and led me to trust You at my mother's breast.

**11** I was thrust into Your arms at my birth. You have been my God from the moment I was born.

**12** Do not stay so far from me, for trouble is near, and no one else can help me.

**13** My enemies surround me like a herd of bulls; fierce bulls of Bashan have hemmed me in!

**14** Like lions they open their jaws against me, roaring and tearing at me.

**15** My life is poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint. My heart is like wax, melting within me.

**16** My strength has dried up like sunbaked clay. My tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth. You have laid me in the dust of death.

**17** My enemies surround me like a pack of dogs; an evil gang closes in on me. They have pierced my hands and my feet.

**18** I can count all my bones. My enemies stare at me and gloat.

**19** They divide my garments among themselves and throw dice for my clothing.

**20** LORD, don't stay far away! You are my strength; come quickly to my aid!

**21** Save my life from the sword, my precious life from these dogs.

**22** Snatch me from the lion's jaws and from the horns of these wild oxen. You have answered me!

**23** I will proclaim Your name to my brothers and sisters. I will praise You among Your assembled people.

**24** Praise the LORD, all you who fear Him! Honor Him, all you descendants of Jacob! Show Him reverence, all you descendants of Israel!

**25** For He has not ignored or belittled the suffering of the needy. He has not turned His back on them, but has listened to their cries for help.

**26** I will praise You in the great assembly. I will fulfill my vows in the presence of those who worship You.

**27** The poor will eat and be satisfied. All who seek the LORD will praise Him. Their hearts will rejoice with everlasting joy.

**28** The whole earth will acknowledge the LORD and return to Him. All the families of the nations will bow down before Him.

**29** For royal power belongs to the LORD. He rules all the nations.

**30** Let the rich of the earth feast and worship. Bow before Him, all you mortal beings — none of whom can keep themselves alive.

**31** Our children will also serve Him. Future generations will hear about the wonders of the Lord.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **22:1-21**: The first half reads like a script of crucifixion written a thousand years before it happened: abandonment, mockery, pierced hands and feet, disjointed bones, divided garments. Whether one reads this as prophecy or pattern, the correspondence is staggering.

- **22:27-31**: The psalm ends not with individual rescue but with global worship. The sufferer's vindication triggers the conversion of 'all the families of the nations' — the scope expands from one person's agony to the redemption of the world.

— PNEUMA
